batches.title: Search-only alias proposals

batches.title: Ambiguity sets — terms that must never auto-resolve
approval_authorizes: Recording that a phrase maps to two or more candidates and must prompt the user

proposals.phrase: Not able to drink or feed at all
proposals.normalized_form: not able to drink or feed at all

provenance.authoring_context: Engineering-authored red-flag display map recording near-miss tokens and the clarification the author believed necessary before escalating.

proposals.ambiguity_notes: Near-miss set for a red-flag token. Source note: Red flag = completely unable to drink/feed. poor_feeding/poor_appetite are milder — use a clarifying question ('Is the person completely unable to drink or feed anything?') before firing emergency, rather than auto-escalating every poor-appetite selection. Escalating a near-miss selection to the red flag changes red-flag reachability and must not be resolved automatically.

proposals.phrase: Shortness of breath
proposals.normalized_form: shortness of breath

provenance.authoring_context: PR #24, merged 2026-07-29, 'picker scoring-gap tokens — 9 fast-follow additions (E9)'. Engineering-authored from kb 2.4 symptom usage. The merge records an engineering deliverable; it records no clinical review.

proposals.ambiguity_notes: 'breathlessness' and 'shortness_of_breath' are BOTH existing canonical scoring tokens. 'breathlessness' carries lower_respiratory_infection(7); 'shortness_of_breath' carries sari(9), asthma(8), cardio_symptoms(7). Mapping one to the other changes which conditions a user can reach and is therefore a clinical-token-identity change, not a search alias. It must not be implemented as an alias. Both tokens remain independent.
lost_context: which of the two distinct tokens the user meant
the condition set reachable from each token differs
